summary: IDS feed c093_nic_span is severely degraded: 2.67 Gbps SPAN source oversubscribes 1 Gbps SPAN destination DIST-SW-02 Gi1/0/48 causing 62.59% pre-tool loss (31,368,720/50,118,720 packets discarded), plus IDS eth1 discards another 3.08% (578,460 packets) due to capture overrun. IDS is blind to majority of traffic.

findings.root_cause: SPAN oversubscription and best-effort copy: DIST-SW-02 Gi1/0/1 mirrors 2.67 Gbps / 50,118,720 packets but SPAN destination Gi1/0/48 is only 1 Gbps. Switch discards 31,368,720 packets on output (100% avg load, bursts higher) = 62.59% lost before broker/tool. SPAN cannot buffer bursts. Additionally IDS eth1 (1 Gbps per tool profile) cannot keep up and discards 578,460 received packets (3.08% tool-side loss), so even delivered traffic is incomplete.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS misses ~62-65% of packets/flows including both directions needed for stateful detection. Signatures, anomaly detection, and file extraction fail on dropped flows; attacker activity easily evades detection, alerts suppressed, forensics incomplete. Tool requires both directions and full payload but receives truncated, lossy feed.

params.broker_requirement: connect TAP to packet broker with buffering then filter/load-balance to fit 1Gbps IDS

recommended_fix.why: TAP provides lossless, non-impacting copy vs SPAN best-effort which drops under congestion. Replacing SPAN eliminates 62.59% switch loss. Because sustained 2.67 Gbps still exceeds single 1 Gbps IDS (hence 3.08% tool drops), broker must then reduce load via filtering irrelevant traffic, or load_balance across multiple IDS sensors, or upgrade IDS capacity to 10Gbps to handle bursts without loss.
